PULL REQUEST TITLE: Import: give the job daemon a queue DSN its parser can read
MERGE MESSAGE BODY:
Observable change: the detached production import can start its job daemon instead of failing immediately with "transport refused: unparseable DSN".

The import requires its queue login to use libpq verify-full TLS, so QUEUE_DATABASE_URL carries sslmode=verify-full and a pinned sslrootcert; the daemon parses DSNs with tokio-postgres, which rejects those parameters. Under POLIS_JOBS_TRANSPORT=tls the daemon now gets the same DSN with only the libpq TLS parameters removed; everything else is kept byte for byte and the derived DSN is never logged. The Python-side verify-full requirement is unchanged, and the daemon still verifies the server certificate (built-in roots off, only the pinned CA trusted, hostname checked, exact host allowlist).

Tests: Python unit tests on the exact production DSN shape; a queue-rs test that the derived DSN parses under TLS and the libpq form is refused. The participant-facing request path is not touched.

PULL REQUEST TITLE: feat(history): persist recent transcripts for copy-back
MERGE MESSAGE BODY:
## Description

When text injection fails, the dictated text is gone — nothing on `main` keeps a copy of what was recognized. This adds a transcript history: every finished dictation session is stored (text, timestamp, engine, model, language, duration) in `~/.local/share/vocalinux/transcript_history.json` and shown in a new "Recent Transcripts" tray submenu. Clicking an entry copies its text back to the clipboard.

Recording happens at the text callback, before injection, so text survives injection failures; the entry is committed on `LISTENING → IDLE` so a session is one entry, not one line per segment.

Persistence is best-effort and privacy-first:

- Writes go through a temp file + `os.replace` (atomic), mode `0600`, under the XDG data dir. A write or load failure logs a warning and keeps going — history can never break dictation.
- The store holds at most `history.max_items` entries (default 10).
- A corrupt file is renamed to `.corrupt` and ignored rather than crashing startup.

Settings → Transcription History has a "Keep Transcript History" opt-out, a "Transcripts to Keep" cap (1–50), and a "Clear History" button. All three apply live: disabling deletes the stored file on the spot, so opting out guarantees nothing is kept anywhere.

Supersedes the in-memory-only approach in #487 (same class name, config section, and tray-menu shape, so it should rebase cleanly either way). Implements the persistence layer specced in VocaHQ/vocamac#23.

## Related issue

Closes #758

PULL REQUEST TITLE: feat(history): add opt-in JSONL persistence for transcripts
MERGE MESSAGE BODY:
## Description

Adds opt-in on-disk persistence to transcription history so a transcript survives an app restart or a failed text injection instead of being lost forever.

- New `history.persist` config (default off). In-memory history stays the default: dictated text should not silently accumulate on disk unless the user asks.
- When on, every snippet is mirrored to `history.jsonl` under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/vocalinux/`, one JSON object per line with timestamp, duration, language, and model when the pipeline reported them. Writes are atomic (temp file + rename) and bounded by the existing `max_items` cap, which is also honored when loading on startup.
- Settings > Transcription History gains a Keep on Disk switch (applies live) and a Clear button. Clear truncates the store; turning persistence off or disabling history deletes it, so "keep no records" holds on disk as well as in memory.
- Malformed lines in the store are skipped on load, and a stale store left behind after persistence was turned off is removed at startup.

Fixes #758

The `retry()` helper in the build pipeline scripts only matched network-level errors (socket hang-up, ECONNRESET, fetch failed, etc.) — not HTTP-level failures. When the Azure DevOps API returns a transient HTTP 500, the code throws `"Unexpected status code: 500"`, which never matched the retry regex, causing immediate failure in steps like "Download Copilot VSIX".

Added `Unexpected status code: 5\d\d` to the retry pattern in `retry.ts`, making all `retry()`-wrapped AZDO calls (artifact downloads, timeline/artifact queries) re-attempt on any HTTP 5xx response using the existing exponential backoff.

## Summary

The agent-CRDT follower's node reconcile path wholesale-replaces a live node's presentation-only state from the CRDT document instead of merging onto it. The document never carries a node's `color`/`bgcolor`/`boxcolor` (renderer-owned fields) or an autogrow input's client-computed friendly label (the readable name shown over a raw dotted slot name like `model.images.image_1`), so any full reconcile — for example the one triggered when a workflow tab goes inactive and becomes active again — blanks a user-picked node color and reverts autogrow input labels to their raw internal names.

This PR adds only failing regression tests (`test.fail` / `it.fails`); it does not include a fix.

## What's here

- `src/workbench/extensions/agent/crdt/graphMutations.test.ts`: an `it.fails()` unit test proving the wholesale-replace directly against `reconcileNode` → `nodeDataStore.updateNode`/`assignNodeFields`, covering both the node's `color` and an input slot's friendly label in one call.
- `browser_tests/tests/agent/agentTabSwitchCatchUp.spec.ts`: a `test.fail()` end-to-end repro alongside the existing tab-switch-reconcile tests in that file. Runs a recorded agent conversation, colors one of its nodes through the real selection-toolbox color picker, opens and returns from a second workflow tab (the real trigger for the full reconcile), and asserts the color survived. It doesn't, and a screenshot of the blanked node is attached to the test result as evidence.

MERGE MESSAGE BODY:
**Stacked on #2702** (base is that branch; retargets to `edge` when it merges).

## Why
The Python poller published a conversation's results as three separate transactions (`math_main`, `math_bidtopid`, `math_ptptstats`), so a crash between them left mixed generations, permanently for a conversation that then went quiet. Recovery scenarios R05 and R09, previously pinned as strict xfails, now pass. Inherited from Clojure's design (`conv_man.clj:158-169`, which is worse: its writes run outside any error handling).

- `database/postgres.py`, `poller/math_writer.py`: tick allocation + all three upserts in ONE `engine.begin()`; fixed lock order (`math_ticks` → bidtopid → ptptstats → main), per-zid rows so two zids cannot deadlock; `write_math_main` is the last statement so a reader never sees `math_main` ahead of its companions; blobs pre-encoded outside the transaction (`encode_math_blob`).
- `poller/service.py`: on load-or-init, unequal `math_tick` across the three rows triggers a full rebuild with a clear log line; a boot-time DB error in that scan is logged and survived (`start()` only; `poll_once` still propagates).
- Tests: R05/R09 xfails removed; R01/R05/R09 negative controls re-pointed for the new write order (assertions preserved); new `test_atomic_publish.py`; `test_start_survives_a_boot_time_scan_failure`.

With Postgres as the search backend, searching for a bare number did not find posts containing that number as the trailing part of a hyphenated word. Searching `12345` missed `check out flight-12345 today`, even though `flight` and `flight-12345` both found it.

Postgres' text-search parser reads the hyphen before a digit run as a **minus sign**, so the digits are indexed with the hyphen glued on:

Terms such as `flight-12345`, `#12345` and `$12345` are not all-digit and are left alone. PULL REQUEST TITLE: [GH-37825] Match signed integer lexemes when searching bare numbers
MERGE MESSAGE BODY:
#### Summary

PostgreSQL's default text search parser lexes a number that follows a hyphenated word as a **signed integer**:

```sql
SELECT alias, token FROM ts_debug('english', 'CVE-2026-2332');
--  asciiword | CVE
--  int       | -2026
--  int       | -2332

SELECT to_tsvector('english', 'We should discuss CVE-2026-2332 here');
--  '-2026':5 '-2332':6 'cve':4 'discuss':3
```

Since #37360 (v11.10) the full identifier `CVE-2026-2332` is searchable again, because the hyphens are preserved and `to_tsquery` produces the matching phrase `'cve' <-> '-2026' <-> '-2332'`. But searching for a bare number that only appears after a hyphen — `2332` — still finds nothing: the query lexeme is `'2332'` while the index holds `'-2332'`.

This PR expands every purely numeric search token (with an optional trailing `:*` wildcard) to also match its signed form, e.g. `2332` becomes `(2332|-2332)`. Tokens inside quoted phrases are left untouched to preserve exact-phrase semantics, and the expansion applies to excluded terms as well, so `-2332` (exclusion) also excludes posts containing `CVE-2026-2332`.

#### Summary

The Clearance attribute shows one set of values in the Membership Policy editor and a different set in Attribute Management, because those two screens are showing two different fields that happen to share a name.

One is a `clearance` **user** field created by Classification Markings' *Enable clearance attribute*, which inherits the classification levels. The other is a plugin-created `Clearance` **template**, with its own options. Attribute Management deliberately hides a template's linked children on the assumption that the template's own row already represents them — but the markings clearance field's template is called `classification`, so its row says nothing about "clearance" anywhere, and the only row an admin can find by searching for it is the plugin's. Policy evaluation was never affected; the enterprise CEL rewrites already compare fields by `linked_field_id`. The confusion is entirely in how the admin UI presents the two, so this fix is webapp-only.

Fields are now told apart by `linked_field_id` rather than by name, through one shared `findNameConflicts` helper so no two screens can disagree about what counts as a conflict. It matches case-insensitively because the server's own uniqueness check is case-sensitive — a template named `Clearance` never collides on the server with a user field named `clearance`, yet an admin reads them as one attribute. MERGE MESSAGE BODY:
## Description

On GNOME Wayland the first dictation left XWayland with a one-group keymap, which broke per-app input-source switching for every X11/XWayland client until relogin (native Wayland apps were unaffected). The culprit: after each scoped IBus injection, `sync_xwayland_layout_from_gnome` (added for #738) re-applied only the single active source via `setxkbmap -layout <one>`, stripping the other layouts and every `grp:` option — so Alt+Shift toggles and the group index mutter drives for Win+Space became no-ops for X clients.

The sync now applies GNOME's complete XKB map — every `xkb` input source in `org.gnome.desktop.input-sources sources` order plus all `xkb-options` — and only when `setxkbmap -query` shows the live rules actually differ, so routine dictation no longer resets the active group on XWayland either.

Also fixed a latent bug in `_read_gnome_input_sources_key`: the `@` type-annotation strip only handled `@a(ss)` and would have mis-parsed `@as []` (empty `xkb-options`), which the new code path reads.

PULL REQUEST TITLE: fix(ibus): sync XWayland layout from GNOME after scoped inject
MERGE MESSAGE BODY:
On GNOME Wayland, Super+Space during a recording can leave XWayland behind GNOME and IBus. The indicator shows `us`, but X apps still type `ru`.

Scoped IBus inject restores `ibus engine xkb:us::eng` and then skips `setxkbmap`, because `restore_xkb_layout` is a no-op on Wayland (#474). That skip is still right for the compositor-owned layout. XWayland just never hears about the new source.

After the IBus restore, copy GNOME's current XKB source (the first `mru-sources` entry) onto XWayland with `setxkbmap` when `DISPLAY` is set. Empty captures are not replayed, and this path does not call `restore_xkb_layout`. Native Wayland sessions with no X display are left alone. The Vocalinux engine is still activated for `commit_text`.

Closes #738

#### Summary
Fix flake in `TestGetLogs` (`server/channels/api4`). Tests-only change; no production behavior changes.

**Root cause:** With `mainHelper.Parallel(t)`, the handler reads the configured log file after `Flush()`, while other goroutines can still append JSON lines. The test asserted that the ten **newest** lines were always the final `Info` batch (`"msg":"10"` … `"msg":"19"`). Interleaved logging makes that window temporarily wrong and breaks `Containsf` on strict numeric messages.

**Fix:** Emit twenty lines tagged with a per-run `model.NewId()` prefix, then use `require.Eventually` (15s wait, 25ms tick) until `GetLogs(0, 10)` returns that tagged sequence. The same length checks and per-line substring assertions remain; pagination calls for page `1` and `(-1, -1)` are unchanged, with closure-local `err2` instead of reusing the outer `Flush` error variable.

**Verification:**
- `go test -run '^TestGetLogs$' -race -count=100 -timeout=25m ./channels/api4/...` — 100/100 green locally.
- The original failure was not reproduced in this environment after 100 stress runs (race-enabled) on the pre-fix test, which matches an intermittent, load-dependent failure; the change targets the identified race between concurrent log writers and the strict “newest page” assumption.

#### Summary

Fix flake in `TestGetLogs` (`server/channels/api4`). Tests-only change — no production behavior changes.

_Requested by **Christian Byrne**_

## Summary

Editing a promoted STRING widget on a subgraph host node was not written back into the subgraph's internal node, so the edit reverted after a disconnect/reconnect of the promoted input.

## Changes

- **What**: The projected host widget's `value` setter and `callback` (`SubgraphNode._projectPromotedWidget`) now write the new value both to `widgetValueStore` (the runtime source of truth for the host display) and back to the resolved interior widget's `value`. The interior widget is already resolved at the widget's only construction site (`_setWidget`), so no extra lookup is needed — it is now threaded through as a parameter.

## Root Cause

A promoted widget's edit only reached `widgetValueStore`. Fully disconnecting the promoted input (e.g. disconnecting and reconnecting the interior link) deletes that store entry (`input-disconnected` → `deleteWidget`), and reconnecting re-registers it seeded from `interiorWidget.value` — which was never updated by the earlier edit — so the host's edit silently reverted to the pre-edit value. This is the same one-way-sync-plus-delete-on-disconnect family as #13601 and #14488.

## Description

The `s_downloaded` cache in `CandidateResolver` was keyed only by `candidateId`, causing stale cache hits when the same `candidateId` is used across different endpoints or local directories. The fix keys the cache by the full `(endpoint, localDir, candidateId)` tuple.

**Change in `CandidateResolver.cs`:**
- Replaced bare `candidateId` cache key with composite key: `$"{endpoint.TrimEnd('/')}|{localDir ?? ""}|{candidateId}"`
- `endpoint` is normalized via `TrimEnd('/')` to avoid collisions from trailing-slash variants

```csharp
// Before — same candidateId from two endpoints shared a cache entry
s_downloaded.ContainsKey(candidateId)

// After — each (endpoint, localDir, candidateId) combination is independent
string cacheKey = $"{endpoint.TrimEnd('/')}|{localDir ?? ""}|{candidateId}";
s_downloaded.ContainsKey(cacheKey)
```

+
+Config loader for optimization-ready Azure AI Hosted Agents. Resolves optimized agent configurations from multiple sources using a priority waterfall:

MERGE MESSAGE BODY:
#### Summary

SVG previews rendered as an empty frame or a "minimal preview image" because `ParseSVG` derived the wrong dimensions, or none at all, and the file preview modal then sized the image from them.

**Server (`imaging.ParseSVG`)**

- `fmt.Sscan` silently accepted relative lengths, so `width="100%"` was stored as `100` pixels. Tools like MarkMap export exactly that.
- The `viewBox` was split on whitespace only, so `viewBox="0,0,800,600"` produced **no** dimensions. (`viewBox="0, 0, 800, 600"` happened to work, because `Sscan` stopped at the comma.)

The modal applied `style={{width: fileInfo.width}}` to every SVG, so a file with no derivable dimensions got `width: 0` and vanished. PULL REQUEST TITLE: Fix broken SVG image previews for files without absolute dimensions
MERGE MESSAGE BODY:
#### Summary

SVG image previews could render as an empty or tiny frame (a "minimal preview image"). This was caused by how SVG size information was handled:

- **Server (`ParseSVG`)** used `fmt.Sscan` to read `width`/`height` attributes, which silently parsed relative values like `width="100%"` as `100` pixels. SVGs generated by tools like MarkMap (which use `width="100%" height="100%"` and no `viewBox`) were therefore stored with bogus `FileInfo` dimensions (e.g. `100x100`). It also failed to read comma‑separated `viewBox` values without spaces (e.g. `viewBox="0,0,800,600"`).
- **Webapp** forced SVGs without known dimensions to a 48px width and into the "small image" container (inline), and to `width:0` (modal), collapsing the preview.

This PR:
- Rewrites `ParseSVG` to prefer the `viewBox`, accept only absolute (unit‑less or `px`) `width`/`height` attributes, ignore relative units such as percentages, and support comma‑separated `viewBox` values.
- Renders SVGs that have no usable pixel dimensions at a sensible size that fills the available preview width, both inline (`SizeAwareImage`) and in the file preview modal (`ImagePreview`), instead of collapsing them.

DRAFT — SCHEMA CHANGE (migration 000031, additive), out of the merge queue until ruled on.

Only active when DELPHI_RESULT_BACKEND=postgres (production is on dynamodb). Observable changes under Postgres, each matching DynamoDB's behaviour:
- pages end where DynamoDB's do (1 MB or Limit) with continuation keys, instead of a flat 1,000-item cap (a 10,000-comment map now returns all its points);
- versions may mix across the pages of one request, as on DynamoDB (before: one version per request, then a 500 if a publication landed between pages);
- each read uses its own short snapshot and returns its connection; the result pool is 8 per process (up to 32 Postgres connections per web process, from 26);
- every read is confined to its conversation and indexed: representative reads drop from ~0.7 s to milliseconds on a production-sized dataset; the participant's next-statement path is no longer starved by long model requests;

PULL REQUEST TITLE: MM-57390: Return error when inviting deactivated users to a team
MERGE MESSAGE BODY:
#### Summary

When a user account is deactivated, attempts to invite them to a team via email now return an error instead of attempting to send the invitation email. Previously, the invitation flow only validated emails against domain restrictions but never checked whether the email belonged to a deactivated account.

**Root cause:** `InviteNewUsersToTeamGracefully`, `InviteNewUsersToTeam`, `InviteGuestsToChannelsGracefully`, `InviteGuestsToChannels`, and `localInviteUsersToTeam` (mmctl) each validated emails only against allowed domain restrictions. None called `GetUserByEmail` or checked `user.DeleteAt` before sending.

**Fix:** For each email in the invite list, after the domain check, the code now calls `GetUserByEmail` and checks whether the returned user has `DeleteAt != 0`. If so, the invite is rejected with a new `api.team.invite_members.account_deactivated.app_error` error, and no email is sent. The change follows the existing per-email error pattern used by graceful invite paths, and mirrors how the `/invite` slash command already excludes deactivated users.

PULL REQUEST TITLE: fix(evdev): skip pointer-motion devices in keyboard discovery
MERGE MESSAGE BODY:
## Description

Why #900 happens: `find_keyboard_devices()` treats any input device with a nonzero `EV_KEY` bitmap as a keyboard, which includes Logitech mice (G502, MX Master 3) whose programmable-button interfaces report key bits. The evdev backend then grabs the mouse node (`EVIOCGRAB`) and re-emits every event, `EV_REL` pointer motion included, through a paired uinput clone. All cursor movement goes through the Python reader thread, which shows up as a periodic cursor hitch (about every 10 seconds in the report) and `SYN_DROPPED` warnings whenever a motion burst overflows the kernel buffer.

Changes:

- `_parse_keyboard_devices_from_proc` now collects the whole device block (name, handlers, `KEY`/`REL`/`ABS` bitmaps) before deciding, and skips blocks that report pointer motion: `REL_X`+`REL_Y` or `ABS_X`+`ABS_Y` set in the low word of the bitmap.
- `_find_keyboard_devices_from_evdev` applies the same exclusion via `capabilities()`, covering the snap-confinement fallback path.
- Wheel-only devices (`REL_WHEEL`) and real keyboards are unaffected, and a mouse's separate "Keyboard" interface node stays monitored, so shortcuts mapped onto mouse buttons keep working.

Skipping the pointer node also removes a quieter problem: a motion flood could overflow the reader's kernel buffer, and the `SYN_DROPPED` recovery then reset per-engine combo state shared by all keyboards.

PULL REQUEST TITLE: fix(evdev): require a real keyboard key in /proc keyboard discovery
MERGE MESSAGE BODY:
## Description

`find_keyboard_devices()` treated any device with a nonzero `B: KEY` bitmap as a keyboard. But almost every input device reports *some* `EV_KEY` code — power and sleep buttons, the ACPI video bus, vendor hotkey blocks, touchpad/mouse buttons, even `ydotoold`'s virtual device. Since v0.18.0's grab-and-suppress change, every such device was `EVIOCGRAB`-grabbed and given a paired `(vocalinux)` uinput clone.

On the reporter's ThinkPad (KDE/Wayland) that produced a full second set of input devices — touchpad, mouse interface, TrackPoint, power/sleep buttons, Video Bus, ThinkPad Extra Buttons, ydotoold's device — and KDE's libinput KCM now sees two logical touchpads, so touchpad settings are silently applied to the wrong one.

This PR applies the rule the evdev fallback path already uses: the KEY bitmap must contain a real keyboard key — a modifier (Ctrl/Alt/Shift/Meta, left or right) or `KEY_A`. Button-only devices never set one, so they stop being discovered, grabbed, and cloned. The mouse "Keyboard" interface nodes that emit real keys (e.g. Logitech G-keys → Ctrl) still qualify, so shortcuts bound to mouse buttons keep working. The #902 pointer-axis skip stays, for mi

The conversation LRU cache (`_convs`) had no lock around the compound lookup → touch → evict sequence. ## Observable change

Participant tokens are now scoped against the conversation resolved by the route, including requests whose query and body name different conversations. A token for another conversation cannot supply its participant ID: membership is resolved for the target conversation and a replacement token is requested. Existing members of invite-only conversations are resolved before first-join restrictions apply.

The ordinary same-conversation-ID path adds no database query. Cross-conversation requests may perform cached conversation resolution, existing authorization reads and an indexed membership lookup; no report, export or external-service work is added to participation.

`server/__tests__/integration/vote-misattribution.test.ts` (23 cases): same-conversation tokens of every kind, cross-conversation tokens, conflicting query and body conversation ids, invite-only existing members, newcomers and owners, participationInit, and OIDC and comment-route controls. `anonymous-jwt.test.ts` now builds its XID participant through the real participation flow.

PULL REQUEST TITLE: [MM-70810] Hide the Posts resource in Global Attributes behind the PostAttributes feature flag
MERGE MESSAGE BODY:
#### Summary

The System Console Global Attributes pages offered **Posts** as an Applies-to resource regardless of the `PostAttributes` feature flag, even though that resource is not finished yet. With the flag off (its default), an admin could add a Posts resource to a global attribute and have linked post fields created for it.

Channels was already gated (on `ChannelAttributes` plus an Enterprise Advanced licence), but that gate was duplicated between the listing table and the details page. This moves it into a shared `useAllowedResourceTypes` hook and adds Posts to it, so both pages offer, fetch, and list exactly the same set of resources:

- **Users** — always offered.
- **Channels** — `ChannelAttributes` flag *and* an Enterprise Advanced licence (unchanged).
- **Posts** — `PostAttributes` flag alone (new).

`fetchAttributeField` and `fetchLinkedFieldsForTemplate` now take the allowed resource types instead of an `includeChannel` boolean, so a scope the server does not offer is never queried. The gating is UI-only; no server behaviour changes.

**QA steps**

1. On a server with an Enterprise licence and `PostAttributes` off (the default), go to **System Console → Attribute Management → Add attribute**.
2. Click **Add resource** in the Applies to card. The menu should offer **Users** only (plus **Channels** on Enterprise Advanced with `ChannelAttributes` on) — no **Posts**.
3. Restart with `MM_FEATUREFLAGS_POSTATTRIBUTES=true` and repeat. **Posts** should be offered again

When one running app has two agent sessions bound to two workflow tabs, the CRDT follower's subscribe target is the session's `boundWorkflowId`. ## Summary

Release the agent panel's `agent.graph-activity` minimap layer in its own unmount hook, so a failing teardown step can no longer leave it registered.

## Before

The layer was disposed as the very last statement of a long `onBeforeUnmount` hook. If any earlier teardown step threw, the dispose call was skipped and the id stayed claimed in the module-level registry. The next time the panel mounted, the registry reported a "Minimap decoration layer exists" duplicate error and handed back a no-op layer, so graph activity silently stopped showing on the minimap. Introduced by #17730.

## After

The layer is released in a dedicated `onBeforeUnmount` hook registered right next to the registration, ahead of every other teardown step. An unmount that hits a throwing step still frees the id, and the next mount registers a working layer without reporting a duplicate.

## Changes

- **What**: `AgentPanelRoot.vue` claims the layer in `onMounted` and releases it in its own `onBeforeUnmount` hook, instead of claiming it in `setup()` and releasing it as the last statement of the large unmount hook. `minimapDecorationRegistry.ts` hands a contested id to the newest claimant and marks the replaced layer disposed, so the outgoing producer's `dispose()` cannot delete its replacement's rows.

#### Summary
Fix flake in `TestGetLogs` (`server/channels/api4`). Tests-only change; no production behavior changes.

**Root cause:** With `mainHelper.Parallel(t)`, the handler reads the configured log file after `Flush()`, while other goroutines can still append JSON lines. The test asserted that the ten **newest** lines were always the final `Info` batch (`"msg":"10"` … `"msg":"19"`). Interleaved logging makes that window temporarily wrong and breaks `Containsf` on strict numeric messages.

**Fix:** Emit twenty lines tagged with a per-run `model.NewId()` prefix, then use `require.Eventually` (15s wait, 25ms tick) until `GetLogs(0, 10)` returns that tagged sequence. The same length checks and per-line substring assertions remain; pagination calls for page `1` and `(-1, -1)` are unchanged, with closure-local `err2` instead of reusing the outer `Flush` error variable.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Public-repo hygiene guard.
+#
+# Usage: scripts/check-public-hygiene.sh <base-ref>
+#
+# Scans the lines ADDED by `git diff <base-ref>...HEAD` and the messages of the
+# commits in <base-ref>..HEAD for references to private working material
+# (internal paths, local home directories, internal tracker ids and names).
+# Prints every hit as `file:line: text` or `commit <sha>: text` and exits 1 if
+# any hit is not listed, as an exact line, in scripts/public-hygiene-allowlist.txt.
+# Exits 0 when there is no unlisted hit, 2 on a usage or git error.
+#
+# Hosted CI runs this same script (.github/workflows/public-hygiene.yml); run it
+# locally before pushing:  scripts/check-public-hygiene.sh origin/edge
+#
+# The patterns below are written with bracket fragments so this file never
+# matches itself.
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+if [ "$#" -ne 1 ] || [ -z "$1" ]; then
+  echo "usage: $0 <base-ref>" >&2
+  exit 2
+fi
+base="$1"
+
+root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
+allowlist_rel="scripts/public-hygiene-allowlist.txt"
+allowlist="$root/$allowlist_rel"
+
+if ! git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${base}^{commit}" >/dev/null; then
+  echo "error: base ref '$base' is not a commit here (fetch it, or check out with full history)" >&2
+  exit 2
+fi
+
+# Matched case-insensitively.
+ci_pattern='agent-cont[e]xt|cost-reducti[o]n/|polis-ast[r]a|polis-clau[d]e|\bast[r]a\b|02-find[i]ngs|04-pl[a]ns|not[e]s/(ops|topics)|dock[e]t|#1[0-9]{3}\b|synth[e]tic'
+# Matched case-sensitively: a macOS home directory. The lower-case form is an
+# API path in this product and is not a hit.
+cs_pattern='/U[s]ers/'
+
+tab="$(printf '\t')"
+tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
+trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
+
+# Each candidate is "<location><TAB><text>"; only the text is matched.
+match() {
+  { grep -iE "${tab}.*(${ci_pattern})" "$1" || true
+    grep -E "${tab}.*(${cs_pattern})" "$1" || true
+  } | sort -u
+}
+
+# 1. Lines added by the diff, as "path:line<TAB>text". The allowlist itself is
+#    skipped: its entries are hits by construction.
+git diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --unified=0 "${base}...HEAD" \
+  | awk -v skip="$allowlist_rel" '
+      /^diff --git / { inhdr = 1; file = ""; next }
+      inhdr && /^\+\+\+ / {
+        file = substr($0, 5)
+        if (file == "/dev/null") file = ""
+        else sub(/^b\//, "", file)
+        next
+      }
+      /^@@ / {
+        inhdr = 0
+        split($0, f, " ")
+        n = f[3]; sub(/^\+/, "", n); sub(/,.*/, "", n)
+        line = n + 0
+        next
+      }
+      inhdr { next }
+      /^\+/ {
+        if (file != "" && file != skip) print file ":" line "\t" substr($0, 2)
+        line++
+      }
+    ' > "$tmp/added"
+
+# 2. Commit messages in the range, as "commit <sha><TAB>text".
+: > "$

+import type {

+  AuthCredential,

+const HEADER_CREDENTIAL = {

+/** The credential kind an auth header carries; `none` when it carries neither. */
+export function authCredentialOf(header: AuthHeader | null): AuthCredential {

+  return headerKey === undefined
+    ? 'none'

#### Summary
Fix flake in `TestCheckTeamsTeamMembersIntegrity` (`channels/store/sqlstore`). Tests-only change — no production behavior changes.

**Root cause:** Integrity checks scan the full database for orphaned `TeamMembers` rows. When sqlstore tests run in parallel, sibling tests can leave orphaned rows in the shared database, inflating global record counts and causing both the empty-report and one-record subtests to fail intermittently.

## Observable changes

- **GET and POST `/api/v3/treevite/waves`, GET `/api/v3/treevite/invites`, GET `/api/v3/treevite/invites/csv`** now return **403** to any caller who is not the conversation's owner or a moderator on the owner's site. Previously any valid token — including an anonymous participant token from another conversation — received 200/201. The admin console, operated by the owner or a site moderator, is unaffected.
- **POST `/api/v3/users/invite`** now returns **403** to the same non-owner callers (previously any signed-in user could send join invitations for any conversation).
- **GET `/api/v3/conversations`** no longer treats an `xid` query parameter specially. Listing conversations no longer creates single-use invite rows as a side effect of the read, and each returned `url` is the ordinary conversation url. No in-repo client sends `xid` to this route.
- **POST `/api/v3/treevite/acceptInvite`** records the accepted invite against a participant that belongs to the requested conversation (creating one when the authenticated user has none there yet) instead of a participant id carried by a token that was issued for a different conversation. Legitimate first-time accepts continue to succeed.

## What changed

The invite-administration routes now apply the same `isModerator(zid, uid)` ownership gate (owner, or a moderator on the owner's site) the data export and conversation UUID routes already use, refusing non-owners before any read or write.

+
+// GET /api/v3/conversations used to create a single-use suzinvite row for every
+// listed conversation whenever an `xid` query parameter was present, and point
+// each conversation's url at the resulting single-use /ot/ join link — a write
+// performed by a read route, with no owner check, recording invitations against
+// the conversation owner. That side effect has been removed: the xid parameter
+// no longer creates suzinvites rows, and the listed url is the ordinary
+// conversation url.
+describe("GET /api/v3/conversations?xid= has no suzinvite side effect", () => {
+  let ownerAgent: Agent;
+
+  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
+  let pool: any;
+
+  beforeAll(async () => {
+    ({ pool } = await import("../setup/db-test-helpers"));
+
+    const ownerUser = getPooledTestUser(
+      RESERVED_POOLED_USER_INDEXES.conversationsXidSuzinvite
+    );
+    ({ agent: ownerAgent } = await getJwtAuthenticatedAgent({
+      email: ownerUser.email,
+      hname: ownerUser.name,
+      password: ownerUser.password,
+    }));
+
+    // Ensure the owner has at least one conversation so the listing is non-empty
+    // (before the fix, each listed conversation produced a suzinvites row).
+    await createConversation(ownerAgent, {
+      topic: "Conversations xid side-effect test",
+      description: "The xid parameter must not create suzinvites",
+    });
+  });
+
+  test("passing xid writes no suzinvites row and returns an ordinary url", async () => {

+

+      "SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS n FROM suzinvites WHERE xid = $1",
+      [xid]
+    );
+    expect(before.rows[0].n).toBe(0);
+
+    // List the owner's conversations with an xid present. This is the path
+    // (no conversation_id) that ran processConversationData, where the side
+    // effect lived: before the fix it wrote one suzinvites row per listed
+    // conversation. The owner has at least the conversation created above.

+    }
+
+    const after = await pool.query(
+      "SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS n FROM suzinvites WHERE xid = $1",
+      [xid]
+    );

+  });

_Requested by **Christian Byrne** · [Slack thread](https://comfy-organization.slack.com/archives/C0A4XMHANP3/p1785484446961109?thread_ts=1785484446.961109&cid=C0A4XMHANP3)_

## Summary

Editing a promoted STRING widget on a subgraph host node was not written back into the subgraph's internal node, so the edit reverted after a disconnect/reconnect of the promoted input.

## Changes

- **What**: The projected host widget's `value` setter and `callback` (`SubgraphNode._projectPromotedWidget`) now write the new value both to `widgetValueStore` (the runtime source of truth for the host display) and back to the resolved interior widget's `value`. The interior widget is already resolved at the widget's only construction site (`_setWidget`), so no extra lookup is needed — it is now threaded through as a parameter.

## Root Cause

A promoted widget's edit only reached `widgetValueStore`. Fully disconnecting the promoted input (e.g. disconnecting and reconnecting the interior link) deletes that store entry (`input-disconnected` → `deleteWidget`), and reconnecting re-registers it seeded from `interiorWidget.value` — which was never updated by the earlier edit — so the host's edit silently reverted to the pre-edit value. This is the same one-way-sync-plus-delete-on-disconnect family as #13601 and #14488.
